clue.text: Bird seen in the sky at night

definitions.text: seen in the sky at night

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher spots something flying overhead after dark.
explanation.definitionFit: The dipper is a small diving songbird of streams, and the Big Dipper is the star pattern of the Plough seen at night.

clue.text: Like mature fruit, or 1 Across upset

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and jumbled, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the answer to 1 Across, the bird, is DIPPER

explanation.surface: Ripe fruit is described, or else a bird is tipped over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or' looks like a link word but it is part of the anagram: OR plus DIPPER, rearranged under 'upset'.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruit ready to fall from the tree when fully ripened is described by this compound adjective.

clue.text: Money on which interest is paid, taking the first place

definitions.text: Money on which interest is paid

explanation.surface: A banker explains the capital sum that earns interest and comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital sum of a loan is the principal, and a person ranked first or chief is also the principal.

clue.text: Way out and without it

parts.note: ex is a Latin-derived word meaning without, as in ex dividend
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sign shows the way out, telling you to leave without something.
explanation.definitionFit: A door marked for leaving a building is a way out, the sense of the sign over it.

clue.text: Pet's accommodation is a place of disgrace

explanation.surface: The family pet's kennel doubles as the place you're sent when you misbehave.
explanation.definitionFit: A kennel for a pet hound has this name, and someone in disfavour is said to be 'in' it.

clue.text: Plain table d'hote

explanation.surface: A plain set menu is on offer at the restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: In old usage an 'ordinary' was a fixed-price meal served at an inn, the same idea as table d'hote.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain means unremarkable or common, and an inn's set meal at a fixed price was historically called by this name.

clue.text: Wherein an author or a civil servant may work

definitions.text: Wherein an author or a civil servant may work

parts.words: Wherein an author or a civil servant may work
parts.note: a writer works from a study in the house, and a British civil servant may work in the government department for policing and immigration

explanation.surface: A writer and a government official share a place of work.
explanation.walkthrough: The UK government department for policing and immigration has the same name as a study kept at home.
explanation.definitionFit: A study kept at home serves a writer, and the British ministry for policing and immigration employs civil servants.

clue.text: Give voice to, out-and-out

explanation.surface: Someone speaks up in absolute terms.
explanation.definitionFit: To speak a word aloud is to say it, and as an adjective the same word means complete or total, as in 'nonsense'.

clue.text: Abstain from extremes of ".excess' and meditate

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters, here taken from excess

parts.note: to chew over something is to meditate on it

explanation.surface: Someone avoids overindulgence and turns to contemplation instead.
explanation.definitionFit: To shun or avoid something deliberately is to abstain from it.

clue.text: Started to ask for article

parts.note: to beg is to ask earnestly for something
an is the indefinite article in grammar

explanation.surface: Someone began by requesting a particular item.
explanation.definitionFit: Commenced, the past tense of start, is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Opening containing gold, provided that diamonds follow

indicators.note: follow puts the diamonds after the gold and the condition in the line of letters

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold
if means provided that, as a condition
ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: A jeweller opens a box of gold with diamonds to come.
explanation.walkthrough: 'containing' is a link here, not a container signal: the pieces run side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A hole or mouth in the body or a vessel is an opening.

clue.text: Of a simple type of writing that's popular

definitions.text: Of a simple type of writing

explanation.surface: A scholar describes a plain style of script beloved of the people.
explanation.walkthrough: Demotic was the simplified cursive script of ancient Egypt, and the word also means of the common people.
explanation.definitionFit: The Egyptian cursive script after hieratic bears this name, and the word also means belonging to ordinary people.

clue.text: Draw off from the leas and :strain.

explanation.surface: A winemaker siphons wine off the sediment and filters it.
explanation.walkthrough: Racking wine is drawing it off the lees, the sediment; to rack is also to strain or torture, as on the rack.
explanation.definitionFit: Winemakers siphon clear wine away from sediment by racking it, and to put something under great stress is to rack it.

clue.text: What one may eat in ocean "voyage?

parts.note: the main is an old word for the open sea
a course is the route a ship sails

explanation.surface: A passenger wonders what will be served at dinner on a sea cruise.
explanation.definitionFit: The principal dish of a meal is the one a diner eats after the starter.

clue.text: Before doing anything else punctually

explanation.surface: Someone promises to deal with a task right away and on time.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something early in the morning or before all other tasks is doing it at the very start of the day.

clue.text: Apple seed to secure

parts.note: a pip is a small fruit seed
to pin something is to fasten it in place

explanation.surface: An apple pip is fastened down.
explanation.definitionFit: Cox's Orange is a named variety of this type of eating apple.

clue.text: Present Public Relations with-a first, advance

parts.note: an offer is the first approach or advance made in a negotiation

explanation.surface: A firm gives its publicity department an early loan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present' is a verb meaning to hold out, not a gift; 'with' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold something out for acceptance is to present or tender it.

clue.text: The words -sent me' are changed by rubbing out

indicators.note: changed means altered in form, so the letters of these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone notes that a phrase has been altered by being erased.
explanation.walkthrough: 'are' looks like the verb of the sentence but its letters join SENT ME as the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The act of erasing or deleting something is a rubbing out.

clue.text: Gas obtained from iron gent

indicators.note: obtained from suggests the letters are extracted and reworked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A chemist extracts a gas from a metal and a gentleman.
explanation.definitionFit: Element number seven makes up most of the air and is an odourless gas.

clue.text: Defer admitting conclusion from champion

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: an end is a conclusion

explanation.surface: Someone puts off letting a champion finish.
explanation.definitionFit: A champion who upholds a cause or title is its protector, and a titleholder in sport defends against challengers.

clue.text: Stretcher providing support?

parts.note: a stretcher here is anything that stretches, and a waistband that stretches holds clothes up

explanation.surface: Ambulance staff carry a patient on a stretcher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stretcher' suggests an ambulance, but it means a material that stretches, as in a waistband holding up trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: A band of stretchy rubbery material stretches and holds garments up.

clue.text: Fight with Eastern leader in a predicament

parts.note: a scrap is a fight or brawl

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here of Eastern

explanation.surface: A fight with an Eastern chief lands someone in trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in an awkward fix or tight spot is a predicament.

clue.text: A vehicle, going over us and a mite

indicators.note: in a down clue, going over places the vehicle above the following word

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
taken as written

explanation.surface: A vehicle runs over two people and a tiny creature.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the genus name for certain mites, tiny arachnids.

clue.text: Wasp in hive, sparkles-

indicators.note: in signals that the letters lie inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A wasp glints inside a beehive.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the Latin genus name for hornets and some wasps.

clue.text: The plain unvarnished truth could be served as 13

explanation.surface: Someone states the blunt facts about what dinner might be.
explanation.walkthrough: 13 is the main course; cold turkey is leftover meat, and 'talk cold turkey' means speak plainly.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means blunt plain speaking in American usage, and leftover roast bird served cold makes a main dish.

clue.text: A saintly race?

parts.note: a classic English horse race at Doncaster, so its name seems to belong to a saint

explanation.surface: A race run by saints is imagined.
explanation.walkthrough: The St Leger is a famous English horse race; read 'St' as Saint and the race seems saintly.
explanation.definitionFit: The Doncaster classic for three-year-olds carries the saint's title 'St' before its name.

clue.text: Measure' boundary

explanation.surface: A surveyor measures out a boundary.
explanation.definitionFit: To dole out or allot is to measure out, and an old legal word for a limit or boundary stone is also this word.

clue.text: An impulse to advise strongly

explanation.surface: Someone feels a strong push to recommend something.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong desire is an impulse, and to press someone earnestly is to advise strongly.

clue.text: Tearing into shreds but it's only horseplay

explanation.surface: Something being ripped apart turns out to be harmless fun.
explanation.definitionFit: To rag something is to tear it to tatters, and student pranks and teasing are called ragging.

clue.text: Forecast that wine is coming to a finish -

parts.note: port is a fortified wine from Portugal
end means finish

explanation.surface: Someone predicts that the wine is about to run out.
explanation.definitionFit: To foreshadow or be a sign of something to come is to forecast it.

clue.text: Send, around a rough steep rock for cheap meat

indicators.note: around means one word is wrapped about the other

parts.note: a crag is a rugged steep rock face

explanation.surface: Someone sends cheap meat around a rocky outcrop.
explanation.walkthrough: SCRAG END is the bony neck end of mutton, a cheap British cut.
explanation.definitionFit: The bony neck end of a sheep carcass is a cheap cut of mutton used in stews.

clue.text: Annoy persistently to make troublesome person hesitate

parts.note: a pest is a nuisance or troublesome person
er is the sound of hesitation in speech

explanation.surface: A nuisance pauses, adding to the annoyance.
explanation.definitionFit: To nag or badger someone over and over is to annoy them persistently.
